The recommended Lincoln Highway improvement is consistent with the goals and objectives of the State's major highway system for the Chicago Metropolitan Area and has been related to various regional and local plans.
B. Maintenance and Enhancement of Long-Term Productivity
Within this planning area, the land use would be altered regardless of a transportation improvement within a determined design time span. Therefore, a transportation improvement within this planning area would have no significant effect upon the long-term productivity.
The recommended improvement of Lincoln Highway is consistent with the goals and objectives of the State's major highway system for the Chicago metropolitan area. The improvement is also consistent with and supportive of the long-range plans of the Villages of Olympia Fields, Park Forest, Matteson and the City of Chicago Heights.
The acquisition of land in the near future may have less of an impact upon the community and the local tax base that would result if acquisitions were delayed to a later date, years in the future. By that time, the required land would be more valuable and the displacements and property damage significantly greater.
The highway investment in right-of-way could be considered a long-term effect since right-of-way investment is usually predicated on a 100-year life span or about four generations. In this context, "long-term uses of man's environment" is taken to mean the period beyond the service of life of the facility.
This proposed highway improvement will effect a safer and more efficient transportation of people, goods, and services, and this in turn will provide the areas with an attractiveness for continuing residential and commercial development.
